clarifications.title: October progress does not give exact query search
clarifications.text: ADGG26 Pelagic Fourier Fishing has one quantum query with success at least 3/4 and randomized cost linear in truth-table length. Its Theorem 1.3 is exact quantum communication for a different problem, with a fixed-degree polynomial classical lower bound. Neither establishes the exponential exact-query separation asked by BK24. AGL26 restricts outputs to a canonical answer with high probability; exact relation algorithms may output many different valid answers.
clarifications.proof_summary: For the upper bound, Fourier sampling chooses y with probability |hhat(y)|^2. Each excluded tail carries less than 1/8 mass, so total success is at least 3/4. A T-query classical algorithm yields a two-way protocol exchanging at most two bits per query to h=fg, transferring the communication lower bound. This verifies the scope/reduction, not every step of the 65-page lower-bound proof.

clarifications.title: Two subquestions with a shared convention
clarifications.text: The first asks whether approximate conical degree can be exponentially larger than approximate relation degree. The second asks whether exact relation degree can be exponentially larger than approximate relation degree. A relation is represented by one nonnegative polynomial per output; their sum is at most one on the whole cube and valid-output mass is at least 1-epsilon on the domain. Exact degree means epsilon=0. Scalar-function or unbounded-off-promise polynomial separations do not suffice.

clarifications.title: Fix both the target and the degree scale
clarifications.text: Definition 59 fixes F_p(x)=+1 when p(x)>=0 and -1 otherwise. Its no-blowup condition is measured against native approximate degree a. Conjecture 72 instead writes polynomial in d=deg(p). For a family, require d=poly(a) with common constants before treating these scales as interchangeable. At zeros, F_p=+1; a replacement approximant need not share those zeros.

clarifications.title: A diagnostic family for the degree mismatch
clarifications.text: On the promise product_{i=2}^n x_i=1, let f_n(x)=x_1 and choose p_n(x)=product_{i=1}^n x_i. Native approximate degree is one, but the chosen polynomial and its fixed natural completion have approximate degree n. Delta=0 satisfies the polynomial-in-d approximant condition. Thus arbitrary p and a native-degree left side cannot be combined literally; this diagnoses a missing degree hypothesis rather than refuting an intended optimal-degree version.
clarifications.proof_summary: Both labels occur on the promise, so no constant approximates f_n; x_1 does. For any polynomial r of degree less than n, orthogonality gives E[r chi_[n]]=0. Uniform approximation to chi_[n] with error below one would instead force this expectation positive. Hence the natural parity completion has approximate degree n.

clarifications.title: Literal unrestricted perturbation is an equivalence of coordinates
clarifications.text: With a full degree-t basis, t>=d, every approximant q to this same fixed F_p has Delta=qhat-phat and p_Delta=q. Conversely such a perturbation already supplies an approximant. This implication needs neither a kernel condition nor Lemma 71. It is an algebraic observation about the literal enlarged-basis statement, not evidence for a stronger restricted characterization.

clarifications.title: A precise sufficient normalization condition
clarifications.text: An editorial sufficient statement, not a replacement author conjecture: q has degree t, full-cube norm at most K, full-cube margin gamma>0 and sign(q)=F_p everywhere. Then fixed-error approximate degree of F_p is O(tK/gamma). To obtain polynomial native-degree overhead, t and K/gamma must be polynomial in a with uniform constants. Keeping only promise signs gives some completion, not necessarily F_p. A coefficient infinity-norm bound alone does not control K.
clarifications.proof_summary: Normalize by K, then compose with a polynomial sign approximant on the two intervals separated from zero by gamma/K. The unrestricted original-support dependent-kernel case remains unverified.

clarifications.title: Verified fixed-edge-size quadratic result
clarifications.text: On the full lambda-partite domain, degree is intrinsic hyperedge-coordinate degree and sensitivity packs disjoint two-edge removal sets. Uniform-fiber averaging and Mobius inversion give 2degree_H<=degree_Z, then the corrected product-permutation cubes yield the quadratic bound.
